title: Virtual-Flow: Virtual Microphone-based Speech Enhancement via Semi-supervised Flow Matching
claim: A pre-trained estimator's output guides a generative model that refines synthesized signals, which then feed a downstream enhancement and beamforming stage.
layout: 1 panel, left-to-right, green box groups the generative module
description: A single wide block diagram reads left to right. On the left, a real multichannel waveform y_r feeds a gray trapezoid pre-trained neural-VME model, which outputs an initial virtual-mic estimate. The estimate acts as a 'Guidance clue' into a green rounded 'Flow matching model' box. Its velocity output goes to an ODE solver, then to a summation node that adds the initial estimate. This yields the virtual-mic waveform. This part sits inside a green-outlined box labeled 'Neural-VME'. Outside the box, the real and virtual signals are concatenated (circled C) and sent to a second gray trapezoid pre-trained MC-SE model. Its output and the stacked signals [y_r, y_v] go into an 'Adaptive Beamformer', which outputs the enhanced waveform. Black arrows and math notation dominate; the green highlight draws the eye first.
caption: Proposed framework for virtual microphone-based beamforming (VM-BF). A pre-trained neural-VME model provides a guidance cue to the flow matching model, enabling precise estimation of the vector field. The VM-noisy speech is reconstructed during both training and inference, thereby enhancing the MC-SE model and improving downstream neural beamforming performance.
abstract: Neural network-based virtual microphone estimation (neural-VME) synthesizes microphone signals at unobserved spatial locations from a limited set of real microphone (RM) physical recordings. This enables high-resolution arrays that improve spatial processing for downstream tasks such as speech enhancement. However, existing methods rely on supervised training with ground-truth signals captured at virtual locations, requiring datasets that scale with the number of virtual microphones (VM) and leaving open the question of how to design optimal large-array configurations. We propose Virtual-Flow, a flow-matching framework that implicitly generates VM signals conditioned on real recordings, without requiring ground-truth VM signals. We introduce a semi-supervised training strategy based on pseudo-VM targets constructed from time-delayed superpositions of real recordings. Virtual-Flow shows improved magnitude estimation in high-frequency bands, yielding richer spatial cues for beamforming. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed Virtual-Flow, combined with reflow distillation, outperforms existing neural-VME baselines in VM-based beamforming and achieves competitive end-to-end speech enhancement performance with low computational cost.
